newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures close up in thin buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures close up in thin buying.

text.p: Rubber futures finished higher on Friday in thin buying with prices buoyed mostly on some shortcovering by Japanese buyers, dealers said. "There were some Japanese buyers engaged in a bit of shortcovering, but the volumes were very thin and this only allowed prices to inch up at the close," a local rubber trader said.
The most heavily traded month in the local exchange was the April/June contract where buyers bought about 450 tonnes, the dealers said.
"It's a weekend market. The buying was very light. Most of the buyers had done their purchases earlier this week," another trader said.
At around 0445 GMT, April/June RSS3 was seen at 131.00-132.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 130.50 cents.
February RSS1 was seen at 179.50-180.50 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.29) a kg from the previous 179.50 cents.
February TSR20 was seen at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.25) a kg from 174.00 cents.
